messages:
maya: Heads-up — after the attn-opt 2.1 compile that went out in canary last night, we see a surge in early-token priming miss rate on the shared fleet. Aggregated prompt hit went 78% -> 66% for 1-8 token prefixes across redwood-3b and rv2-7b-4bit. Anyone else seeing this?

simon: Saw the same on the dashboard. Latency ~stable but token cost and miss-rate spiked. Looks correlated with the compile window around 03:10 UTC.

olga: Uploading a couple flamegraphs and a short trace paste below. Main hotspot is in key serialization paths.

perf-bot: Quick summary: canary window 03:10-04:00 UTC — early prefix hit rate delta -12ppt, sample size ~120k requests. Top stack: serialize_prefix_keys -> warmup_victim_lookup -> fused_attn_dispatch.

jun: Can we check whether hash_salt or key encoding changed in the new kernels? Run I did quick grep on the build artifacts: `rg "hash_salt|kv_key_encode" -n build/attn-opt-2.1` -> shows an incidental bump in salt constant in commit `d3f4a2`.

ci-bot: Deploy log snippet: `2026-03-16T03:12:45Z canary: attn-opt-2.1 rollout start; kernel-fallback: enabled; target: 10% of canary nodes`. No runtime flags for key normalization were set.

simon: Hypothesis: attn-opt picks a fused-attn kernel path that serializes KV keys with a different byte-order/packing than legacy. Warmup seeding writes key prefixes under the old format, read path expects new format -> misses. Mixed batches (small prefix + long context) trigger fused path more often, so small-prefix priming suffers.

olga: Flamegraph snippet (pseudo):
```
serialize_prefix_keys  34%
warmup_victim_lookup   18%
fused_attn_dispatch    12%
batch_coalesce         9%
other                  27%
```
Shows heavy time spent preparing keys rather than hit lookups.

maya: Do we know if warmup seeding is firing? We depend on short-prefix seeding (1-8 tokens) to prime KV entries before the main decoding loop.

simon: Warmup is still enabled but the batcher change in the compile groups short prefixes into mixed-size batches which route to the fused kernel. Fused kernel currently omits the previous canonicalization step.

jun: Quick mitigation test: forced a subset of canary nodes to legacy kernel with `--force-kernel=attn-legacy` for 2 hours. Result: early-prefix hit rate recovered to ~80% (baseline 78% -> 80%). Means canonicalization difference is the likely culprit.

maya: OK — options: (A) immediately rollback attn-opt 2.1 in canary and stop rollout, (B) add normalization shim so both kernels produce/consume canonical keys, or (C) change batcher heuristics to avoid fused path for short prefixes.

olga: I'm going to open a PR with a minimal canonicalization shim that runs at the lowest cost (same code path used by legacy) and add a unit/regression test that exercises short-prefix warmup seeding. Will also add a perf regression test in the nightly harness.

simon: Plan of record: 1) pause further attn-opt rollouts (rollback in canary), 2) land normalization shim asap, 3) add a CI regression that compares pre/post key serialization for both kernels, 4) re-run canary with instruments.

jun: I'll instrument a 60m wall profiler across canary nodes and collect hot keys + key sizes. Also adding a temporary metric `kv_key_mismatch_rate` emitted from warmup checks.

perf-bot: Created perf ticket INF-1723 and attached canary traces.

ci-bot: Rollback started at 04:05 UTC for attn-opt-2.1 canary (subset).

maya: Thanks. Olga/jun/simon — please sync on PR + rollback validation. I'll notify support and customer success for any noisy accounts. :eyes:

olga: Will post PR link and a small repro harness after initial test passes.

simon: Adding a quick checklist: 
- [x] pause rollout
- [ ] land normalization shim
- [ ] add CI regression
- [ ] verify in canary
- [ ] safe resume rollout

jun: I'll follow up with logs + profiler output once collected.

maya: 👍 keeping this thread as the single source for action items.
